## 953db766893d

**Finding: suspected curriculum/domain shortcut, not a reproduced validator bug.** A strong rival is: identify the regular wall lattice; color a zero room `4` iff it crosses a mostly-wall lattice row or column through an opening (a “merged lattice cell”), otherwise color it `3`. This explains all four public canonical profiles and matched 2,000/2,000 sampled generated inputs (500 in each of `None`, easy, medium, and hard) because the present lessons realize larger rooms by deleting internal wall segments rather than independently varying size. The deterministic sample receipt is `checks/audit/sample-probes.json`.

The exact counterexample is `checks/audit/953db766893d/input.json`: an intact 2×2 wall lattice with two 3×3 minimum rooms and two 3×5 larger rooms. The rival colors all four rooms `3`, stored in `checks/audit/953db766893d/rival.json`. The selected rule colors the two 3×3 rooms `3` and the two 3×5 rooms `4`, recorded by the supported Racket apply command in `checks/audit/953db766893d/racket.json` (rule hash `d815686e5b33`, generator SHA-256 `e006889235c3c44c137c1c6b26e103fe20cad4f4e1935358f0a9d8107783f792`).

The input does **not** pass the current `self_check`: it is rejected because the finite declared scene-profile tuple does not include an intact 2×2 lattice with four rooms. It is nevertheless a direct lawful instance of the selected size-coloring rule. Therefore this is best classified as an under-taught broader-domain distinction. No source was changed because this was an audit-only target.
